description:
Waveshare ESP32-P4-WIFI6-DEV-KIT in Raspberry Pi form factor.
Uses the ESP32-P4NRW32 or ESP32-P4NRW32X (dual-core RISC-V @ 400MHz, 16MB flash, 32MB PSRAM).
The ESP32-P4 has no built-in radio; Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth are supported through the onboard ESP32-C6 co-processor.
100M RJ45 Ethernet (with optional PoE using a hat), MIPI DSI display and MIPI CSI camera connectors, microSD slot,
3.5mm audio jack plus onboard microphone and amplified speaker header, I2C/I3C headers, RTC battery header,
USB-A OTG (jumper-switchable), USB-C USB serial adapter and Serial/JTAG ports, 28 user GPIOs.
The GPIO pins use the Raspberry Pi 40-pin header layout, and some Raspberry Pi hats are compatible.
Different revisions of the ESP32-P4-WIFI6-DEV-KIT may use engineering samples or production variants of the ESP32-P4.
Several bundles were available, including additional components:
**ESP32-P4-WIFI6-DEV-KIT-A:** Waveshare RPi Camera B.
**ESP32-P4-WIFI6-DEV-KIT-B:** Waveshare RPi Camera B, Waveshare 7-DSI-TOUCH-A Display.
**ESP32-P4-WIFI6-DEV-KIT-C:** Waveshare RPi Camera B, Waveshare 10.1-DSI-TOUCH-A Display.

Also sets up a light component for controlling the display backlight.

featured_bundles.name: Waveshare 10.1-DSI-TOUCH-A Display (display and backlight control)

featured_components.description:
Onboard ESP32-C6 running ESP-Hosted over SDIO gives the radio-less ESP32-P4 Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth.
The wifi and esp32_ble components only work while this is present.
featured_components.name: ESP32-C6 wireless co-processor

featured_components.description: Built-in IP101 Ethernet PHY (RMII) — selected automatically when a device is created without Wi-Fi credentials.
featured_components.name: Onboard Ethernet

featured_components.description:
Onboard "BOOT" button.
Conflicts with Ethernet (GPIO35 is used for Ethernet PHY TXD1).
featured_components.name: BOOT Button

featured_components.description:
The shared I²C bus used for onboard components (Audio codec),
and available for external devices via the I²C connector,
MIPI SCI and DSI connectors,
and SDA/SCL pins on the 40pin header.
This will also allow you to use some Raspberry Pi hats with I²C peripherals.
Onboard components support max frequency 400kHz.
If you connect additional peripherals, you may need to reduce the frequency.
featured_components.name: Onboard / Shared I²C bus

featured_components.description:
Set up an SPI bus on the 40pin header corresponding to Raspberry Pi SPI0.
This will allow you to use some Raspberry Pi hats with SPI peripherals.
Use this for hats where SCLK is on header pin 23 (RPi GPIO11),
MISO is on header pin 21 (RPi GPIO9),
and MOSI is on header pin 19 (RPi GPIO10).
The SPI CS will be on GPIO36 (header pin 24 / RPi GPIO8)
or GPIO32 (conflicts with I³C connector – header pin 26 / RPi GPIO7).
featured_components.name: Raspberry Pi GPIO header SPI0 bus

featured_components.description:
Set up an SPI bus on the 40pin header corresponding to Raspberry Pi SPI1.
This will allow you to use some Raspberry Pi hats with SPI peripherals.
This SPI bus conflicts with the microSD power supply and audio amplifier control.
Use this for hats where SCLK is on header pin 40 (RPi GPIO21),
MISO is on header pin 35 (RPi GPIO19),
and MOSI is on header pin 38 (RPi GPIO20).
The SPI CS will be on GPIO22 (header pin 12 / RPi GPIO18),
GPIO21 (header pin 11 / RPi GPIO17),
or GPIO46 (header pin 36 / RPi GPIO16).
featured_components.name: Raspberry Pi GPIO header SPI1 bus

featured_components.description:
An I²C bus that allows you to read/write the information EEPROM on Raspberry Pi HATs.
Conflicts with the USB-C Serial/JTAG/OTG connector.
featured_components.name: Raspberry Pi header HAT ID I²C bus

featured_components.description:
Use the I³C connector as an I²C bus to attach additional peripherals.
This I²C bus will also be available on the 40-pin header GPIO33 and GPIO32 (SDA and SCL, respectively).
featured_components.name: I³C connector as I²C bus
